title: Tech 06 Backup Retention
decision: Choose a backup and retention policy under recovery objectives and cost limits.
context: A SaaS product stores transactional data and customer-uploaded documents.
The current policy keeps daily full backups for one year.
Storage growth is increasing backup cost rapidly.
constraints: Database RPO must be at most 15 minutes.
Database RTO must be at most 2 hours.
Monthly backup storage cost must fall by at least 35 percent.
options: Keep daily full backups for a year and negotiate storage pricing.
Use continuous log backup plus weekly fulls, tier older backups, and test restores.
Reduce retention to 30 days for all backup types.

evidence.fact: Daily full database backups account for 72 percent of current backup storage cost.
Point-in-time recovery logs average 6 percent of the storage consumed by a daily full backup per day.
Compliance requires recoverability of month-end records for 12 months but not daily full images.
The last quarterly restore drill recovered a weekly full plus logs in 76 minutes.
Cold-tier storage costs 68 percent less per GB but has a retrieval delay of up to 20 minutes.
Document objects are versioned independently and already use lifecycle tiering, so the database policy is the dominant remaining cost lever.
